questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A patient had a possible HIV exposure 10 days ago and an initial test is negative. Which response is most accurate?
choices: The negative result permanently excludes HIV
Testing may be within the window period; follow the diagnostic algorithm and arrange NAT or repeat testing when indicated
Begin lifelong ART without additional evaluation
Only an antibody differentiation assay can detect every acute infection
questions.explanation: A negative test obtained early may occur during the window period. Exposure timing, test type, symptoms, and PEP or PrEP use guide follow-up testing, including NAT when acute infection is suspected.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes HIV viral load from CD4 count?
choices: Viral load estimates immune function, while CD4 measures kidney function
Both values always change at the same rate
Viral load measures circulating virus and treatment response; CD4 estimates immune function and opportunistic-infection risk
CD4 alone confirms medication adherence
questions.explanation: HIV RNA viral load is the primary marker of virologic response. CD4 count describes immune status and helps guide selected opportunistic-infection prevention; the trends are related but not interchangeable.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which presentation in a patient with advanced HIV most strongly suggests possible Pneumocystis pneumonia?
choices: One week of progressive dyspnea, dry cough, fever, and exertional or resting hypoxemia
An isolated ankle bruise after a fall
Sudden ear pain with normal oxygenation
Chronic constipation without respiratory symptoms
questions.explanation: PCP commonly presents subacutely with progressive dyspnea, nonproductive cough, fever, and hypoxemia. Modest lung findings do not exclude serious gas-exchange impairment.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which precaution is appropriate when providing routine care to a stable patient with HIV and no other suspected infection?
choices: Airborne isolation solely because of HIV
Contact isolation for the entire admission
Standard Precautions, with Transmission-Based Precautions only if another condition requires them
No gloves for anticipated blood exposure
questions.explanation: HIV alone does not require special isolation. Standard Precautions apply to all patients, and additional precautions are chosen for another suspected or confirmed transmissible infection.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A nurse sustains a needlestick from a used hollow-bore needle. What is the priority action?
choices: Squeeze the wound and apply bleach
Wait for the source patient's final tests before reporting
Wash with soap and water, report immediately, and begin the exposure evaluation
Finish the shift and report the injury tomorrow
questions.explanation: Immediate cleansing and reporting start a time-sensitive exposure assessment. Caustic chemicals and wound squeezing are not recommended, and evaluation should not wait until the end of the shift.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which plan best reflects current HIV post-exposure prophylaxis principles when PEP is indicated?
choices: Start as soon as possible, ideally within 24 hours and no later than 72 hours, then complete the prescribed 28-day course
Delay treatment until every source test is final
Start any time within two weeks and stop after symptoms resolve
Use one dose only if baseline testing is negative
questions.explanation: PEP is time-critical and should begin as soon as possible without waiting for all pending results. The usual indicated course is 28 days with regimen-specific monitoring and follow-up testing.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which patient statement demonstrates accurate understanding of U=U?
choices: An undetectable result means HIV has been cured
Sustained undetectable viral load prevents sexual transmission of HIV, but I still need ART and routine care
U=U also prevents every sexually transmitted infection and pregnancy
I can stop ART as soon as my first viral load is undetectable
questions.explanation: Sustained viral suppression prevents sexual HIV transmission. It is not a cure, does not remove the need for ART and monitoring, and does not prevent other infections or pregnancy.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A previously suppressed patient now has a detectable HIV viral load. What is the best nursing response?
choices: Label the patient noncompliant and end teaching
Tell the patient to double every ART dose
Explore adherence, access, adverse effects, interactions, absorption, and possible resistance without blame
Assume the laboratory result proves AIDS
questions.explanation: A detectable or rebounding viral load requires confirmation and systematic assessment of barriers, tolerability, interactions, absorption, and resistance. Nonjudgmental inquiry supports safer, more effective care.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A patient develops fever and worsening lymph-node symptoms soon after starting ART for advanced HIV. Which interpretation is safest?
choices: This always proves ART failure
IRIS is possible, but new or uncontrolled infection, toxicity, and treatment failure must also be evaluated urgently
The patient should stop ART independently
The symptoms are expected and never need assessment
questions.explanation: IRIS can unmask or worsen inflammatory manifestations after ART begins, but it is a diagnosis requiring comparison with active infection, drug toxicity, and treatment failure. Therapy changes belong to the treating team.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which finding in a patient with a low CD4 count requires the most urgent evaluation?
choices: New severe headache, confusion, and a focal neurologic deficit
A request to review a vaccine record
Stable appetite with unchanged weight
A healed abrasion
questions.explanation: Acute neurologic change may reflect opportunistic CNS infection, stroke, malignancy, seizure, or another emergency. Airway and neurologic stabilization and urgent diagnostic evaluation take priority.
